coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Rock Block D2
record.summary: The site of Mission Rock's only permitted stand-alone parking structure, a 100-ft-max garage on the Bridgeview Street side of Block D sized in the EIR at about 2,300 spaces (837,200 gsf) to replace Giants event parking. It is the one element the Port names as part of Phase 2, whose Garage Report was submitted in October 2022 before the phase was decelerated in 2023.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one (see digitization_method): treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines. The D1/D2 line is a land-use zone boundary inside one Design Controls block, not a lot line; the Appendix marks Block D's parcel dimensions as illustrative.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco / Mission Rock Partners, adopted April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m. D1/D2 split from Figure 1.1 (p.10) and the Block D standards sheet (Appendix p.190).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so joining status.csv to it would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Structured Parking per the D4D's Land Use Plan -- a flat 100 ft max height (not a 90-110 ft range as sometimes described), with no upper/tower zone. Occupies the larger, eastern portion of the combined Block D parcel (D1 is the smaller residential tower at the 3rd St corner; see that entry). A 2016 EIR cites roughly 2,300 parking spaces project-wide across two garages (not confirmed as D2 alone). The Central District Energy System was tentatively planned for Parcel A, not Block D, per a 2019 Mission Rock Partners submittal to the Port -- despite some secondary summaries placing it here.

facts.value: Structured parking only: the Design Controls permit stand-alone above-grade parking nowhere else at Mission Rock, and no residential, production, commercial or retail uses on D2

About 2,300 in the EIR (with up to 700 more in a possible below-grade garage under Mission Rock Square); the DDA describes 3,000 structured spaces project-wide to serve the project and ballpark patrons
97,498 (2.24 acres) for Block D as a whole, D1 and D2 combined
Bridgeview Street and Mission Rock Street; driveways for the shared parking facility permitted here
Until built, Lot A (the remaining Seawall Lot 337 lot) holds 1,000 to 1,500 cars and Pier 48 up to 750 to 1,000 for Oracle Park events
Port of San Francisco (Seawall Lot 337); future parcel to be ground-leased for 75 years under the DDA
Seawall Lot 337 Associates, LLC (San Francisco Giants and Tishman Speyer), master developer with an option on each vertical parcel
Phase 2 submittal delivered December 2022 but decelerated in 2023 as infeasible; the Port's October 2023 repayment model used a hypothetical Phase 2 start of March 2026

open_questions: The Garage Report's actual space count and levels are not in the Port memo; the report itself was not located.
The geometry file's note that a 2019 submittal placed the district energy plant on Parcel A rather than Block D is confirmed by the July 2019 Phase 1 overview and the September 2019 budget memo.

No construction start, Phase 2 budget approval or vertical design submittal for this block was found in Port Commission agendas through February 2026; the block remains part of the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot (Lot A).
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.
The DDA 'Outside Dates' for commencing later phases are in the DDA itself, which was not read.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block D2. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The DDA itself (lodged with the Board of Supervisors 2/1/2018, Board File 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18, effective 8/15/2018) places Parcel D2 (the garage) in Phase 2 in its Land Use Table (DDA Section 1.5) and its Exhibit B2 Schedule of Performance gives a 2018 'Target Date' of May 2023 for completing Phase 2's horizontal Phase Improvements -- already elapsed with Phase 2 not begun, and the Outside Date for actual completion is left to a future Phase Schedule that was never approved (Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023, per this record's own milestones). No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 2 or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a non-elapsed date for this block.

2026-09-21 pass: the June 9, 2026 Port Commission item (Resolution 26-34, $10M pre-development investment) updates the earlier finding below that no Port memo gives a revised target year -- Port staff now have a schedule for Phase 2 pre-development work (through Fall 2027 contractor procurement) and a 'potential' construction start as early as Summer/Fall 2027, but the memo explicitly frames 2027/2028/2029 as alternative scenarios depending on when the Developer secures anchor tenants, not a single committed date -- still no basis (record, phase or project) for an expected-completion milestone for this block specifically.
